title: Sammy Davis Jr: National Treasure
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant (with guest producer Dylan) profile entertainer Sammy Davis Jr., covering his childhood in vaudeville with the Will Mastin Trio, his Army years and fights with racists, his rise via Frank Sinatra and the Las Vegas Sands, losing his left eye in a 1954 car crash and converting to Judaism, his marriages (Kim Novak affair, Laurie White, Mai Britt, Altovise Gore), JFK disinviting him from the 1961 inauguration, his support for Nixon and Vietnam USO tour, Rat Pack years, Church of Satan involvement, the Poor Devil pilot, tax debts, and his death from throat cancer in 1990. The episode ends with listener mail about calling 911 with a fake pizza order as a silent distress signal.
topics: Stuff You Should Know listener mail

segments.title: Opening banter and Billy Crystal's Oscar blackface
segments.summary: Hosts open with tour dates and banter, then discuss Billy Crystal's Sammy Davis Jr. impression, including blackface at the 2012 Oscars, and Davis's early life as a child performer in blackface.

segments.title: PBS American Masters documentary and USO tour
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the PBS American Masters documentary on Davis and his 1972 USO tour of Vietnam, where he performed for soldiers with minimal staging.

segments.title: Poverty, lack of schooling, and early shielding from racism
segments.summary: Key formative factors: childhood poverty, touring vaudeville instead of attending school and learning to read late, self-consciousness about it, and being shielded from racism until he joined the Army.

segments.title: Army years and fighting racism
segments.summary: In the Army Davis confronted racism directly and fought white racists, having his nose broken at least twice. After a fight, a defeated opponent told him he was still black, which shaped his decision to fight prejudice through performance.

segments.title: Will Mastin Trio, Las Vegas, and Frank Sinatra
segments.summary: After the Army he returned to the Will Mastin Trio, which began playing Las Vegas. Sinatra had them open for him there. Black performers were barred from staying or gambling in the hotel and had to use back routes, and Davis was later barred from the Sands pool until it was drained and refilled.

segments.title: Spinal Tap reference and Zeros breakthrough
segments.summary: Brief Spinal Tap tangent about Davis's memoir Yes I Can, then the hosts describe the break at Zeros (now the Comedy Store) where Davis's impressions of white celebrities, including Cary Grant, led to a Hollywood breakthrough and a William Morris contract.

segments.title: Losing an eye, Sinatra's help, and conversion to Judaism
segments.summary: Davis lost his left eye in a 1954 car crash and relearned movement with help from Sinatra. A hospital visit from a rabbi started his interest in Judaism, which he converted to, calling himself a one-eyed black Jew.

segments.title: Loyalty to the Will Mastin Trio and marriages
segments.summary: Davis kept a three-way profit split with his father and uncle for fifteen years. The hosts then discuss his relationships: dating across race lines, the reported threat tied to Kim Novak, the forced breakup, his marriage to Laurie White, and his marriage to Mai Britt.

segments.title: JFK disinvitation, civil rights, and Nixon
segments.summary: Kennedy personally had Davis disinvited from the 1961 inauguration over his marriage to a white woman, while Harry Belafonte remained. Davis later supported Nixon, who welcomed him, and he marched in Selma and gave money to civil rights causes. He was also in the Rat Pack and performed in the Ocean's Eleven film.

segments.title: Listener mail on 911 pizza code and sign-off
segments.summary: A listener mail reply from responder Brooke Diane explains that 911 dispatchers will ask callers who order pizza whether they dialed the wrong number, and can then send help. The hosts sign off.
